pass_a_gloss: Logos 2. [Lemma, Isaiah 2:1:] The word that came from the Lord to Isaiah, son of Amoz, about Judaea and about Jerusalem. Akin to the things before are the things set before us, and someone would see them coming through the equal thoughts, having set a fine mind upon the insights of the meaning. For the words came of old from God to the divine prophet about Judaea and about Jerusalem. And it seems somehow to have a middle and not very clear rendering of the vision, to say about Judaea and about Jerusalem. But as is possible we will make clear the very force of the vision, as it were bringing it together briefly into mind. For since he tries to speak of the laying waste of the perceptible Judaea and of Jerusalem, but of the showing forth of the [one] in Christ and spiritual, and of the manifestation in this world; for the sake of this cause, not on behalf of Judaea, nor yet against Jerusalem, but about Judaea and about Jerusalem he says to have beheld the vision. And perceptible we say the Judaea, and indeed also Jerusalem, the very country in which Israel dwelt, and the very body of the synagogue of the Jews. And spiritual again Jerusalem, or Judaea, we hold to be the Church, or the circumcision in spirit, that is, those having in Christ the circumcision not made by hands in mind and heart. And indeed one of the holy prophets called out to the Jews: Be circumcised to God, and circumcise your hardness of heart, men of Judah and those dwelling in Jerusalem. And the divine Paul knows another Jew, not the one according to flesh rather, but the one in spirit. For he writes thus: For not the one in the open is a Jew, nor the circumcision in the open in flesh, but the one in the hidden a Jew, and circumcision of heart, in spirit, not letter, whose praise is not from men but from God. It is needed therefore soberly to watch when the prophet makes words against Jerusalem, or Judaea, and when about the [one] in Christ and spiritual, which also truly is perfect and blameless. What then does he say? [Lemma, Isaiah 2:2-3:] That in the last days the mountain of the Lord will be manifest, and the house of God upon the tops of the mountains. And it will be lifted above the hills, and all the nations will come upon it. And many nations will go, and will say: Come, let us go up to the mountain of the [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: Logos 2. “The word that came from the Lord to Isaiah son of Amoz concerning Judah and concerning Jerusalem” (Isaiah 2:1).

What lies before us is akin to what came before, and anyone who fixes a careful mind on the insights of its meaning would see that it moves through the same ideas. For the words came long ago from God to the inspired prophet concerning Judah and concerning Jerusalem. Yet the vision seems somehow to be expressed in a middle way, and not very clearly, when it says “concerning Judah and concerning Jerusalem.” Still, we will make plain the force of the vision as far as we can, gathering it briefly, as it were, into view.

He is trying to speak of the laying waste of the visible Judah and Jerusalem, but also of the showing forth of the spiritual one in Christ and of her appearing in this world. For this reason he says that he saw the vision not on behalf of Judah, nor yet against Jerusalem, but concerning Judah and concerning Jerusalem.

By the visible Judah, and Jerusalem too, we mean the land itself in which Israel dwelt, and the very body of the synagogue of the Jews. The spiritual Jerusalem, or Judah, we hold to be the Church, that is, the circumcision in the Spirit: those who have the circumcision made without hands in Christ (Colossians 2:11) in mind and heart. So one of the holy prophets cried out to the Jews: “Be circumcised to God, and circumcise your hardness of heart, men of Judah and you who dwell in Jerusalem” (Jeremiah 4:4). And the divine Paul knows another Jew, not the one according to the flesh but the one in the spirit, for he writes: “For he is not a Jew who is one outwardly, nor is circumcision that which is outward in the flesh; but he is a Jew who is one inwardly, and circumcision is of the heart, in the spirit, not in the letter; his praise is not from men but from God” (Romans 2:28–29).

So we must watch soberly for when the prophet speaks against Jerusalem, that is, Judah, and when he speaks concerning the spiritual one in Christ, which is truly perfect and blameless. What then does he say? “For in the last days the mountain of the Lord shall be manifest, and the house of God on the tops of the mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills, and all the nations shall come to it. And many nations shall go and say: Come, let us go up to the mountain of the…” (Isaiah 2:2–3).
